text:
AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Recover Username.
To recover a username, the agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, then verifies identity with 3 of these 4 items: full name, zip code, phone number and email address. Usernames are the first letter of the first name, the last name and the number 1, for example John Smith becomes jsmith1.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Recover Password.
For a forgotten password, the agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and the username (if the username is unknown, the Recover Username steps come first). The agent cannot see the old password but can generate a new one after the customer gives either the PIN number or the answer to the security question.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Reset Two-Factor Authentication.
To reset two-factor authentication, the agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account. A reset code is sent to the customer's email address. If the customer cannot use the email, they give their PIN number or answer the security question (mother's maiden name) and the code goes to the email on file. The agent also sends a link about security best practices.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Service Added (unknown service on the account).
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, records how the customer heard about it (email, spouse or news) and checks the system. If there is no error: an email was a scam not sent by the official AcmeCorp marketing team, and a spouse or the news was misheard or misunderstood, with no extra charges. If the error is real, the service is removed and a $40 refund is offered.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Service Removed (service lost by mistake).
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, records how the customer heard about it and checks the system. If the customer is right, the service is reinstated and the agent checks that it works; it may take a few minutes to appear. If not, the customer misheard or the email was a scam.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Free International Shipping Question.
For questions about free shipping to or from another country, the agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, checks the account in the system and sends the customer a link to the subscription FAQ page.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Missing Credit.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and asks where the credit came from: a subscription refund, a previous purchase or a promotional package. If the system shows the credit is not missing, it is a display problem and the customer should log out and back in. If it is missing, the agent adds it with a promo code; the standard amount is $40 when the customer does not know.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Change Address.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, asks for the current street address (street part only), verifies identity with 3 of 7 items (zip code, phone number, PIN, username, password, email address, order ID of a previous purchase) and then enters the new street address.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Change Name.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, asks for the current first and last name, verifies identity with 3 of 7 items (zip code, phone number, PIN, username, password, email address, previous order ID) and updates the account with the new name.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Change Phone Number.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, asks for the current phone number in the format (XXX) XXX-XXXX, verifies identity with 3 of 7 items and then saves the new number in the same format.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Change Account Payment Method.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, asks for the current payment method, verifies identity with 3 of 7 items and sets the new method. The valid payment methods are credit card, debit card and PayPal.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Unexpected Fee on an Order.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order with full name, account ID and order ID, and checks whether the company made an error. A company error means the fee is removed. Otherwise Gold and Silver members still always get the fee removed, while for Bronze and Guest members the fee stays.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Delivery Time Change.
When a customer wants the delivery moved from morning to evening, the agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order (full name, account ID, order ID), checks the system for an error and the shipping status, then updates the order. Simply confirming a date belongs to the shipping status flow.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Wrong Payment Method on an Order.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and verifies the order. If the order is Order Received or In Transit, the payment method can be changed immediately to credit card, debit card or PayPal. If it is Out for Delivery or Delivered, the new method only applies to future orders.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Wrong Quantity in the Confirmation Email.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order and checks the system. If the email was wrong, the customer was only charged for one item. If it was a company mistake and the order is Order Received, the refund is offered and the extra item removed; once shipped, the customer waits for delivery and calls back.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Upgrade to Overnight Shipping.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order and asks for the shipping status. Only an order at Order Received can be upgraded; once shipped it will likely arrive today or tomorrow anyway. Gold members have the fee waived; Silver, Bronze and Guest members pay $20 on the card on the account.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Downgrade to Next-Week Delivery.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order and checks the shipping status. If not shipped, the delivery can move to next week. If already shipped, Gold, Silver and Bronze members get the shipping fee credited back, and Guest members cannot be helped.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Add an Item to an Existing Order.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order and checks the shipping status. At Order Received the item (brand and type, e.g. Guess Jeans) is added directly. If already shipped, Gold and Silver members get the new item in a separate order with no shipping fee.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Accidental Duplicate Item.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order and checks the shipping status. At Order Received the refund is offered and the duplicate removed. If shipped, Bronze, Silver and Gold members get a refund right away and call back later for a shipping label; Guests wait for delivery and call back.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Initiate Refund.
The agent asks for the refund reason and for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account. The purchase is validated with username, email address and order ID. The customer picks a refund method: gift card, add value to the account, paper check or credit card; a gift card or paper check needs the full mailing address, the others the account ID. The agent then offers the refund amount, which defaults to $50 if the customer does not know it.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Update Refund (add an item to an existing refund).
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, validates the purchase with username, email address and order ID, and records the brand and type of the new item. The new total refund is the previous refund amount plus the price of the new item.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Refund Status.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, then validates the purchase by collecting the username, then the email address, then the order ID. Only a verified record can show the status, which is one of: not started, in progress or complete. If the customer is unhappy with the status, the agent escalates it to a manager.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Returns (stained item, wrong color or wrong size).
All three return reasons follow the same steps. The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and validates the purchase (username, email address, order ID). Eligibility depends on membership: Gold members get unlimited returns; Silver within 6 months, or with a receipt, or in the original packaging; Bronze within 90 days, or with a receipt, or in the original packaging; Guest within 30 days or with a receipt. If eligible, the agent takes the full address for the shipping label and the customer chooses by mail, in store or drop-off center.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Bad Price (competitor cheaper or lower price yesterday).
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, records whether the reason is a competitor or yesterday's price, and verifies the order ID. The agent explains that pricing algorithms change prices dynamically, outside the agent's control. If the customer keeps pushing, the agent offers a promo code.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Many Items Out of Stock.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, writes a report for the Purchasing Department so they can do a better job, and offers a promo code if the customer is still unhappy.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. One Item Out of Stock.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, records the item, reports it to the Purchasing Department and can back-order it with the card on file; it ships as soon as it is available.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Promo Code Invalid or Out of Date.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and checks the code. Promotions typically last 7 days, so an older code is out of date. If the code should work, the problem is fixed; if the customer used it wrongly, Gold, Silver and Bronze members get a new code for 20% off their next purchase, while Guests cannot be helped.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Mistimed Billing (sent back or never bought).
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and validates the purchase. For an item already sent back, waiting more than 7 days is a valid error and the credit is processed; before 7 days only Gold members get it. For an item never bought, if the system says it was the customer's error, only Gold members get the credit.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Shipping Status Question.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies the order and checks the system. The shipping statuses are Order Received, In Transit, Out for Delivery and Delivered. To fix a problem the agent can change the date, the address, the item or the price.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Change a Shipment (address or wrong item).
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, checks the shipping status, validates the purchase and then updates the order with the new shipping address or the correct item.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Missing Package.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and validates the purchase. Within 7 days a package can be marked delivered by mistake and may still arrive in a couple of days. After a week or more the agent ships a new order using the full address and the brand and type of the product.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Shipping Cost Complaint.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, validates the purchase and checks the shipping status. At Order Received or In Transit the shipping fee can be waived. At Out for Delivery or Delivered only the standard shipping amount of $8 is refunded.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Product Questions (boots, shirts, jeans, jackets).
Questions about a specific product are answered from that product's FAQ page: there are FAQs for boots, shirts, jeans and jackets. The agent searches the FAQ and selects the matching answer. The article texts themselves are not part of our guideline documents.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Storewide Questions (pricing, membership, timing, policies).
General store questions are answered from the storewide FAQ, which has four categories: pricing, membership, timing and policies. The agent searches the FAQ and selects the matching answer; the article texts are not part of our guideline documents.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Subscription Status, Amount Due and Due Date.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies identity and checks the subscription: active or cancelled, the amount due and the due date. The agent can also send a link so the customer can log in and check it.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Pay a Subscription Bill.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account, verifies identity, checks the amount due and takes the payment. The standard subscription is $99 a year; without a card number the card on the account is used.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Subscription Payment Extension.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and checks the membership level. Gold members can always get an extension, Silver members only when 1 day late, and Bronze and Guest members cannot; the agent can then pass their phone number to a manager who calls back.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Dispute a Subscription Bill.
The agent first asks for the customer's full name or account ID to pull up the account and checks the membership level. Gold members always get what they ask for, Silver members get a refund when the wrong amount is under $10, and for Bronze and Guest members it depends on the system check. The refund is the difference between the correct and the billed amount.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Credit Card Rejected on the Website.
The customer can re-enter the card details, log out and back in, and check the card's expiration date. If nothing works, the agent can place the purchase using the card number, expiration date and the item's brand and type.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Shopping Cart Not Updating.
The customer can refresh the page and add the item again, log out and back in, and check whether the item is out of stock (shown at the bottom left of the product page). If nothing works, the agent can place the purchase for them.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Search Not Working.
The customer can log out and back in, clear the browser cookies (browser settings, More Details) and try a different search such as Prada Handbag before the original item. The agent reports the problem to the website team and can place the purchase if needed.

AcmeCorp support policy handbook. Website Too Slow.
The agent reports the slowdown to the website team. The customer can log out and back in, close other tabs and programs, and try another website: if every site is slow, it is their internet connection, not AcmeCorp.
